verdict.reason: The script depiction of an open vessel fire, flare gun ignition, and aerial fireworks in S010-S011 is accurate, but the cited excerpts provide only title/scope headings and truncated intro text from CSATF Safety Bulletins #13, #16, and #19. They fail to state or entail any operative rules, coordinator/licensing mandates, specific Coast Guard or Fire Marshal permit requirements, or marine firefighting apparatus and spotter boat procedures.

claim_checks.quote: Scenes S010 and S011 depict the firing of a practical marine flare gun into diesel-soaked blankets on a wooden boat, completely engulfing the Margaret Rose in a massive open blaze at night on navigable waters, followed by the ignition of a commercial mortar fireworks array.
claim_checks.reason: Accurately describes the depicted events across scenes S010 and S011.

claim_checks.quote: The shoot requires an experienced, state/federally licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator / SFX Coordinator to design controlled burn rigs, propane/gas flame bars, or practical flame effects, rather than uncontrolled liquid accelerants.
claim_checks.reason: The cited excerpts do not contain operative text mandating a licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator/SFX Coordinator or specifying flame bars over liquid accelerants.

claim_checks.quote: Production must secure written marine burn permits from the local Fire Marshal / Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and the U.S. Coast Guard, and deploy dedicated marine firefighting apparatus, spotter safety boats, and charged fire suppression equipment.
claim_checks.reason: The excerpts only provide introductory scope text and do not establish requirements for specific written permits from the USCG/Fire Marshal or dedicated marine firefighting craft and apparatus.

claim_checks.quote: Engage a licensed Special Effects / Pyrotechnics Coordinator to engineer controlled flame rigs, safe ignition systems, and regulated aerial mortar effects.
claim_checks.reason: No operative excerpt is provided establishing the coordinator requirement or engineering standards for these effects.

claim_checks.quote: Obtain formal burn permits and marine event authorization from the local Fire Marshal and U.S. Coast Guard.
claim_checks.reason: General compliance language in citation [2] does not establish specific permit or authorization mandates from the USCG or local Fire Marshal.

claim_checks.quote: Position dedicated fire safety craft with water pumps, manned suppression hoses, and safety buffers during all rehearsals and takes.
claim_checks.reason: The cited excerpts do not specify or require dedicated marine fire safety craft, water pumps, manned hoses, or buffer zones.
Depiction of large-scale open vessel fire, accelerants, and fireworks justifies a high hazard flag.

claim_checks.quote: Open vessel burns and aerial pyrotechnics carry substantial fire propagation, smoke inhalation, toxic byproduct, and explosion risks. The shoot requires an experienced, state/federally licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator / SFX Coordinator to design controlled burn rigs, propane/gas flame bars, or practical flame effects, rather than uncontrolled liquid accelerants. Production must secure written marine burn permits from the local Fire Marshal / Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and the U.S. Coast Guard, and deploy dedicated marine firefighting apparatus, spotter safety boats, and charged fire suppression equipment. Remedy costs vary based on jurisdiction permitting fees, burn vessel preparation, and SFX crew size

The shoot requires an experienced, state/federally licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator / SFX Coordinator to design controlled burn rigs, propane/gas flame bars, or practical flame effects, rather than uncontrolled liquid accelerants.
